title: Licensing Revenue Recognition - ASC 606
learning_objectives: Distinguish right to use vs right to access

right_to_access.description: Customer entitled to access IP as it exists throughout license period (IP changes over time and customer benefits from changes)
indicators: Entity continues to be involved with IP (updates, upgrades, support)
Customer's ability to derive benefit depends on entity's ongoing activities
IP has significant standalone functionality that will change
examples: Brand name license where entity actively promotes brand

right_to_use.description: Customer entitled to use IP as it exists at point in time (IP substantially exists, customer can use independently)
indicators: IP has significant standalone functionality at point of license
Customer can benefit from IP independently
Entity not required to perform ongoing activities that significantly affect IP

decision_framework.step_1: Does license provide right to use or right to access?
decision_framework.step_2_if_right_to_use: Recognize revenue at point in time (license grant)

sales_based_royalties.exception: Sales-based or usage-based royalties on licenses of IP: Recognize revenue when later of (1) subsequent sale/usage occurs, OR (2) performance obligation satisfied/partially satisfied
sales_based_royalties.example: License software with 5% royalty on customer's sales. Recognize royalty revenue as customer makes sales (not upfront).

upfront_fees_and_usage_fees.upfront_nonrefundable: If right to use: Recognize when IP available. If right to access: Defer and recognize over term.
upfront_fees_and_usage_fees.minimum_guarantee: If minimum guarantee plus usage fees: Allocate and recognize based on pattern (typically over time for minimum, as usage for excess)

calculation_example_right_to_use.facts: Grant perpetual software license for $100K. Customer downloads software Jan 1. No ongoing support.
calculation_example_right_to_use.analysis: Right to use (standalone functionality, no ongoing involvement)
calculation_example_right_to_use.accounting: Recognize full $100K revenue on Jan 1 (DR AR $100K, CR Revenue $100K)

calculation_example_right_to_access.facts: Grant SaaS subscription $12K for 12-month access. Ongoing updates and support.
calculation_example_right_to_access.analysis: Right to access (customer benefits from ongoing updates)
calculation_example_right_to_access.accounting: Defer and recognize ratably: $1K per month. Jan 1: DR AR $12K, CR Unearned Revenue $12K. Monthly: DR Unearned Revenue $1K, CR Revenue $1K.

calculation_example_royalty.facts: License patent with 10% royalty on licensee's sales. Year 1: Licensee sales $500K. Year 2: $600K.

accounting.year_1: Royalty = $500K × 10% = $50K. DR AR $50K, CR Royalty Revenue $50K (when sales occur)
accounting.year_2: Royalty = $600K × 10% = $60K. DR AR $60K, CR Royalty Revenue $60K

combined_with_other_goods_services.separate_performance_obligations: If license distinct from other goods/services, separate performance obligation (allocate transaction price)
combined_with_other_goods_services.not_distinct: If license integral to other goods/services, single performance obligation
combined_with_other_goods_services.example: Software license plus implementation services. If distinct: Allocate. License at point in time (if right to use), services over time.

functional_vs_symbolic_ip.functional: Has standalone functionality (software, patents, formulas) → Typically right to use
functional_vs_symbolic_ip.symbolic: Derives value from association with entity (brand, logo, franchise name) → Often right to access if entity supports brand

cpa_exam_tips: Right to use: Point in time (license grant). Right to access: Over time (license period).
Indicators of right to access: Ongoing involvement, IP changes, customer benefits from changes
Indicators of right to use: Standalone functionality, no ongoing involvement required
Sales-based royalties: Recognize when sales occur (not upfront)
SaaS subscriptions: Typically right to access (recognize over time)

classification_decision: 1. Does entity have ongoing involvement that significantly affects IP?
2. Does IP change over time and customer benefits from changes?
3. If yes to above → Right to access (over time)
4. If no (standalone functionality, no ongoing involvement) → Right to use (point in time)

common_scenarios.perpetual_software: Right to use → Point in time
common_scenarios.patent_license: Right to use → Point in time (usually)
common_scenarios.franchise_without_support: Right to use → Point in time

common_mistakes: Recognizing SaaS revenue upfront (should recognize over time)
Recognizing sales-based royalties upfront (should recognize as sales occur)
Not distinguishing right to use from right to access
Forgetting to evaluate ongoing involvement and IP changes

key_points: Right to use: Point in time (license grant). Right to access: Over time (license period).
Right to access: Ongoing involvement, IP changes, customer benefits from changes
Right to use: Standalone functionality, no ongoing involvement
Sales-based royalties: Recognize as sales occur (not upfront)
SaaS: Typically right to access (recognize over time)
Perpetual software: Typically right to use (recognize at grant)
